title: Detach to Primitive
summary: Block detaches to stock tldraw primitives (measured off the live DOM, not a ported layout function) and rebuilds back to the live component — card position/size and a port dot's center measured at 0px offset across all three BlockView variants, after finding and mutation-verifying a real 24px coordinate-frame bug and a real ~20px cross-host DOM-scoping bug.
intro: Zach's brief (PROJECT - Black Box UI.md, "Detach to primative" section): a story per component showing before / detached / rebuilt, stock tldraw primitives only, and near-pixel-perfect matching with an adversarial loop over the numbers. This report leads with the numbers that loop produced.

Scope this pass: Block (rendered as BlockPort in this app's scene model) across its three BlockView variants (simple / port / expanded), with Port's own detach defined and exercised as the sub-primitive Block composes per port — exactly the hierarchical rule Zach asked for. glyph/code/value node kinds are real, scoped-out follow-up (see "Outstanding" below), chosen deliberately over doing all four roughly.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/hosts/tldrawHost.tsx — one additive prop, onEditorReady?(editor, container), fired once at the end of the existing handleMount; nothing else in the file changed (17 insertions, 2 deletions, verified with git diff --stat)

docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — new src/detach section citing every donor line the kit ported from packages/adapter-tldraw/src/detach/* (this repo, frozen v1) and stating plainly what was NOT ported and why
findings: Card position/size, before→detached and before→rebuilt (round trip): 0px offset on every axis (dx, dy, dw, dh), all three BlockView rows — measured by pnpm test-stories's own play function, not eyeballed
Port 'in' dot center, before→detached and before→rebuilt: 0px offset, all three rows — see the offset table below for the two real bugs this number caught before it read zero
Stock-only assertion: every shape the detached column paints enumerates as tldraw's own geo/text/group types — never a custom ShapeUtil — asserted mechanically per row, not by inspection

Full baseline preserved: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p . clean; unit project 39 files / 725 tests (was 38/721, +1 file +4 tests, all mine); storybook project 60 files / 259 tests, all green with STORYBOOK_PORT=5519

Both real bugs the adversarial loop caught are mutation-verified (reverted the fix, watched the exact symptom reproduce, restored it) — see the offset table and block.ts/editorContainer.ts's own WHY comments

Context-menu wiring ("Rebuild" appearing in tldraw's right-click menu) is NOT done — see Outstanding. It needs a second additive change to tldrawHost.tsx beyond the one this lane was authorized to make, and I would rather say so than ship unwired or unverified UI code

sections.heading: The adversarial loop — every round, in the reviewer's own words
sections.html:
Round 1 — 24px, every row, both columns. dx=24 dy=24 dw=0 dh=0 on the card, identical across simple/port/expanded and identical for detached AND rebuilt. Root cause: every box block.ts measures off the DOM is relative to the node's own wrapper element (starts near (0,0)), but lowerToGroup creates the replacement primitives as SIBLINGS of the original shape in its PARENT's frame — so a wrapper-relative box has to be shifted by the original shape's own (x, y) before it means anything there. The donor (blockPrimitives.ts) does this with an explicit origin parameter added to every box; this port's first draft dropped that addition. One shapes.map(p => ({...p, x: p.x+shape.x, y: p.y+shape.y})) fixed every row at once — fixed the round trip too, since it shares the same code path.

Round 2 — port dot ~20px off, port/expanded rows only. Card was already 0px; the port-level check (added specifically because the card alone doesn’t prove label/text placement, which is what Zach named as the actual complaint — "I don’t like how when you convert there are these pixel offsets") showed the 'in' dot's ring landing at the CARD's vertical centre instead of its rail position, for BOTH the port and expanded rows, at the exact same y (94.125px) in both. Two different views producing the identical wrong number was the tell: not a geometry bug, a DOM-SCOPING bug. Root cause: shapeIdForNode is deterministic per scene-node id, and this gallery's 9 cells all reuse the node id "proc" — so document.querySelector('[data-shape-id="shape:bbox-proc"]') matched whichever of the 9 mounted hosts happened to render first in DOM order, not the host actually being detached. Fixed by editorContainer.ts: a small registry mapping each live Editor to its own DOM container (populated once via the new onEditorReady seam), so every query scopes to the right host.

Round 3 — confirmed real, not a timing race. Before finding the scoping bug, a first hypothesis was that BlockPort's rail geometry (measured off the header/body boundary, per that file's own "Measurement (D-A5)" section) simply hadn't settled yet when the detach fired. Built a real settle-wait (waitForPortDotsToSettle, 3 consecutive identical dot-position readings over real wall-clock time, not just animation frames) and reran — IDENTICAL 20px number. That ruled out timing and pointed straight at the cross-host contamination above.

Mutation verification, both fixes: reverted the coordinate-frame shift → the story failed with expected 24 to be less than or equal to 6 on every row, exact symptom reproduced. Restored it, confirmed green again. The scoping fix's mutation is recorded the same way in editorContainer.ts's own header (the 94.125px collision, reproduced with debug logging before the fix, gone after).

Every number above is the literal output of pnpm exec vitest --project=storybook run -t Block's own console.table(offsets) in the play function (DetachToPrimitive.stories.tsx) — not retyped from memory. Tolerance kept at 6px in the assertion (not tightened to match the measured 0px) because these fixtures use short, single-word labels; a longer label could still show the system-sans-vs-tldraw's-bundled-Plex-Sans metric difference stockShapes.ts's header documents. Chasing that residual further with the fixtures on hand would be measuring noise, not fixing a bug.

stories.title: Blocks / Detach To Primitive — Before / Detached / Rebuilt
stories.look_for: 3 rows (simple/port/expanded BlockView) x 3 columns (before/detached/rebuilt). The card reads dark/low-contrast in every column, before included — that is tldraw's own dark-mode filter over its embedded HTML layer (tldrawHost.tsx's pre-existing, documented behaviour, not something this lane changed); getComputedStyle confirms the card's real background is white in both 'before' and 'rebuilt', identically. Look at the port dots, the divider line under "proc", and the ring/label placement instead of the card's apparent shade.
